c.tagline: Gateway to Angkor's ancient temple kingdoms.

taxi.fareNote: Tuk-tuks and taxis negotiate fixed fares upfront (no meters); typical in-town ride $2-4, day of temple touring by tuk-tuk $15-20

emergency.note: Tourist Police: 097 778 0002 / 012 402 424; response times can be slow outside central areas, private clinics (Royal Angkor International Hospital) recommended for serious issues

hood_landmark.Riverside/Old French Quarter: Preah Ang Chek Preah Ang Chorm Shrine, Siem Reap
hood_landmark.Svay Dangkum: Park Hyatt Siem Reap, Svay Dangkum

avoid.reason: Generally safe; touts around Angkor and tuk-tuk overcharging

hood_desc: The backpacker and nightlife hub around Pub Street and the Old Market, packed with restaurants, bars, massage shops and markets; best for first-timers who want everything walkable.
A leafy, laid-back riverside area a short walk/tuk-tuk from downtown with boutique guesthouses and good local restaurants; suits travelers wanting quiet nights but easy access to town.
A quieter residential-feeling area near the river north of downtown, popular with mid-range and boutique hotel guests seeking a calmer base still close to the action.
A rapidly developing strip southwest of downtown known for its concentration of budget hostels and value guesthouses; suits backpackers and budget travelers.
The upscale, garden-hotel enclave with Siem Reap's luxury resorts set among rice paddies northeast toward Angkor; suits honeymooners and travelers wanting a resort escape.

water.note: Not safe to drink from the tap; use bottled or filtered water, though commercial ice at tourist restaurants is usually fine.

transit.pay: Cash (USD or riel) paid directly to the driver; tuk-tuks and taxis are agreed by fixed fare before the ride, the small public bus network takes cash fares onboard. No rechargeable transit card system exists.
transit.hours: Tuk-tuks/taxis operate roughly 24 hours via hotels and apps; public buses run daytime hours only, roughly 5:30am-8pm
transit.note: There is no rail or metro system; nearly all visitor transport is by tuk-tuk, private car, or bicycle

train: Royal Railway Phnom Penh-Poipet line stops at Siem Reap (limited passenger service)
ferry: Seasonal boat to Tonle Sap floating villages/Phnom Penh via Tonle Sap Lake (dry-season dependent)

airport.name: Siem Reap–Angkor International Airport (SAI)
rentals: No major international rental counters on-site; cars typically hired with driver via hotels/agencies

tip.r: Not obligatory but appreciated; rounding up or 10% at restaurants and small tips for tuk-tuk/guide services are common
